title: The Best Used SUVs Under $20,000 in 2026
summary: These days you won’t find a mainstream manufacturer without at least one SUV in its lineup. We think for $20,000 you can find a very good one, but which is right for you? We've chosen the used SUVs that should be on your list.
body_markdown:
Shopping for a midsize SUV or crossover can feel like navigating a maze—dealership lots are packed with options, and narrowing down the right choice takes real effort. The answer ultimately comes down to your specific needs. Are you after a three-row family hauler, a trail-ready compact, or a model loaded with the latest tech and top safety ratings? Whatever your priorities, the right SUV exists.


The catch? New vehicle prices have never been higher, with the average new car now hovering near the $50,000 mark.


Here's the silver lining: the used SUV market is overflowing with exceptional vehicles ready for a second chapter. Depreciation can dramatically reduce prices—even on low-mileage examples—giving budget-focused buyers outstanding value. With $20,000 to work with, your options are broader than you might think. Below are our top picks across a wide range of SUV categories.

## Toyota RAV4 Hybrid


**Best Fuel-Efficient SUV Under $20,000:** Toyota RAV4 Hybrid **Priced from:** $15,000


We'd love to steer you toward a Lexus RX 450h within a $20,000 budget—and technically, it's possible. But you'll be looking at one with well north of 100,000 miles. The smarter move at this price point is the Toyota RAV4 Hybrid Limited, which delivers most of what the Lexus brings to the table, and within this budget you can realistically find one with fewer than 70,000 miles on the odometer.


In the $15,000 to $20,000 range, expect to be shopping RAV4 Hybrid Limited models from around the 2016 model year. What makes the RAV4 such a compelling choice is its sheer versatility—it's equipped to handle almost anything life demands, short of hauling more than four additional passengers. The Mitsubishi Outlander plug-in hybrid and Nissan Rogue are also worth considering in this space, though finding lightly used examples within this budget is trickier.


The RAV4 Hybrid Limited arrives well-equipped from the factory, with leather upholstery, the largest available touchscreen, a power sunroof, and heated seats. The hybrid powertrain also delivers class-competitive fuel economy, rated at 34 mpg city and 30 mpg highway by the EPA.

## Kia Sportage


**Best Compact Crossover Under $20,000:** Kia Sportage **Priced from:** $16,000


A $20,000 budget can unlock some surprisingly recent used vehicles, and the Kia Sportage is a standout example. You won't be getting into a top-tier trim, but if the LX in cloth with all-wheel drive (AWD) suits your needs, you can find a 2023 Sportage LX AWD with under 50,000 miles—potentially with some factory warranty still in effect. It's also worth knowing that Kia covers non-certified used models with a five-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty.


Having spent considerable time behind the wheel of this compact crossover and its Hyundai platform-mates, we can confirm it's a genuinely solid vehicle. One consistent criticism: rearward visibility is notably restricted. The generously sized backup camera display and standard blind-spot monitoring go a long way toward compensating, but the compromised rear sightlines are something to keep in mind during your test drive.


That quibble aside, the Sportage is a capable, dependable, and comfortable crossover packed with standard safety technology. It's more than capable of moving a small family through the demands of everyday life without missing a beat.

## Ford Edge


**Best Used Midsize Crossover Under $20,000:** Ford Edge **Priced from:** $13,000


Searching for midsize crossovers under $20,000 turned up some genuinely attractive Ford Edge Titanium examples enrolled in Ford's certified pre-owned (CPO) program. Expand your search across trim levels and you'll uncover CPO Edges in a variety of colors and configurations, particularly in front-wheel drive (FWD). The Chevrolet Equinox competes in the same space but doesn't keep pace with the Edge on features at this price.


The Titanium sat at the top of the Edge range alongside the performance-oriented ST, above the SE and SEL. In practice, the SEL is the trim you'll encounter most frequently on the used market. It's well-equipped—alloy wheels, leather seating, power-adjustable seats, automatic climate control, Bluetooth, and heated seats are all included—though it stops short of the premium touches that define the Titanium. If those extras aren't essential, the Edge is a genuinely refined, hushed, and comfortable everyday companion.


It also hits a proportional sweet spot. The Ford Explorer has ballooned in size over the years, while the Ford Escape can feel a touch too snug—the Edge sits right in between.

## Subaru Outback


**Best AWD Crossover Under $20,000:** Subaru Outback **Priced from:** $15,000


The Subaru Outback began its life as a station wagon, but today it stands fully established as a crossover SUV in every meaningful sense. In fact, previews of the 2026 model suggest the Outback will finally shed the last remnants of its wagon DNA altogether.


Standard AWD has long made the Outback—much like its Forester sibling—a go-to choice for drivers in the snowy Northeast, the Pacific Northwest, and throughout the Rocky Mountain region. Subaru has refreshed the Outback repeatedly over the years, steadily expanding interior space for passengers and cargo alike while advancing its suite of safety technology with each generation.


The 2.5-liter flat-four found in most Outbacks may leave performance-minded drivers or high-altitude commuters craving a bit more, but it's a smooth, well-matched unit paired to a continuously variable transmission (CVT). Combined with the Outback's capable AWD system, it makes for a well-rounded package for anyone who regularly faces harsh weather. Drivers wanting more power could opt for the available 3.6-liter H6 or, in later models, a turbocharged 2.4-liter four-cylinder.


New Outbacks now start near $30,000 and climb well past $40,000, but previous-generation examples deliver the same rugged character and most of the same mechanical substance at a significantly lower cost. Starting from the 2015 model year, there's no shortage of quality options available under $20,000.

## Lincoln MKT


**Best Large Crossover Under $20,000:** Lincoln MKT **Priced from:** $18,000


We've steered countless family-hauler shoppers toward the Ford Flex over the years, and those who followed the advice have come back nothing but pleased. The Lincoln MKT shares its bones with the Flex but trades that vehicle's boxy, armored-truck silhouette for a more polished, upscale look.


Like the Flex, the MKT largely flew under the radar during its production run. Many examples ended up in livery fleets after Lincoln retired the Town Car. Part of the issue was a lofty MSRP when new—but the used market has corrected that dramatically. For $20,000, you can find a meticulously maintained, fully loaded, low-mileage MKT complete with a heated steering wheel, backup camera, navigation, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, lane departure warning, and more. The MKT brings luxury-level appointments typically associated with far pricier SUVs, making it one of the most underappreciated values in the used market today.


One important note: Given the MKT's history in livery service, always pull a vehicle history report and arrange a pre-purchase inspection—regardless of how spotless the listing appears. Fleet operators tend to stay current on maintenance, but verifying that firsthand is always worth the effort.

## Jeep Renegade


**Best Compact Rugged SUV Under $20,000:** Jeep Renegade **Priced from:** $16,000


A patient shopper can track down a Jeep Renegade Trailhawk with under 30,000 miles for less than $20,000—and it's absolutely worth the search. We had reservations about small Jeeps before the Renegade came along, but this model genuinely shifted our perspective. That said, it doesn't quite reach the interior polish of the larger Cherokee.


Built on the same platform as the Fiat 500X, the Renegade wraps that foundation in a taller, more squared-off hatchback body with a scrappy personality and those signature circular headlights. Under the hood is a four-cylinder engine mated to a nine-speed automatic—a cut above the CVTs that dominate this segment. And despite its compact footprint, it's a legitimately capable off-roader. You won't be tackling the Rubicon Trail, but reaching a remote campsite is comfortably within its abilities. For outdoors-minded buyers on a budget, it's a hard package to beat.

## Chevrolet Tahoe


**Best Full-Size SUV Under $20,000:** Chevrolet Tahoe **Priced from:** $18,000


Twenty thousand dollars can put you behind the wheel of a Chevrolet Tahoe with fewer than 100,000 miles—though it requires some digging. GMT800-era examples are plentiful at this price, but the more desirable target is a GMT900 from the 2007 to 2014 model years. These trucks look sharp, ride comfortably, and deliver a genuinely spacious, capable experience.


Browsing CarGurus listings, we found several solid examples from around 2011, most in LT trim—which brings leather seating, wood-grain accents on the dash, center console, and door panels, along with the comfort features you'd expect from a full-size SUV. The one notable omission is a moonroof, but that's a minor trade-off given everything else on offer.


These are extraordinarily durable machines, built to reach 250,000 miles with proper maintenance. Find a clean example with 75,000 miles on the clock and there's a real possibility your kids will be borrowing the keys when they get their license.

## Jeep Wrangler Unlimited


**Best Fun SUV Under $20,000:** Jeep Wrangler Unlimited **Priced from:** $12,500


Stretching your budget from $15,000 to $20,000 opens up the Jeep Wrangler market considerably. That additional five grand makes it far more realistic to step into a four-door Unlimited, which brings substantially more rear passenger space and enough cargo room to carry more than a single overnight bag.


The $20,000 mark tends to be the dividing line between high-mileage and more reasonable examples. A Wrangler Unlimited listed at $19,995 will likely arrive with a soft top and around 90,000 miles, while spending $22,000 typically gets you a hard top and closer to 75,000 miles.


Certain trims will also remain out of reach at this price. A Rubicon is unlikely to fall within the $20,000 ceiling, but a Willys is a realistic find—and it delivers much of the same rugged character and off-road hardware in a slightly more attainable package.

## BMW X3


**Best Luxury SUV Under $20,000:** BMW X3 **Priced from:** $13,000


The BMW X3 occupies an ideal position within BMW's lineup—compact enough to feel nimble, yet spacious enough to be genuinely useful day-to-day. It delivers the interior quality, driving refinement, and sporting character of a 3 Series, while adding the elevated ride height and cargo flexibility of a compact crossover. It holds its ground convincingly against rivals from Volvo, Acura, Mercedes-Benz, and Audi.


At $20,000, you're looking at models from around 2016 with just over 60,000 miles—relatively modest for a luxury SUV of that vintage. The high-performance X3 M is off the table at this price, but the X3 xDrive28i delivers brisk acceleration, sharp handling, and a surprisingly roomy interior for a vehicle this sporty.


One insider tip: If you're open to the first-generation X3 built between 2006 and 2010, the value proposition becomes extraordinary. These can be had for considerably less, and models fitted with BMW's naturally aspirated N52 inline-six—specifically the 3.0si and xDrive30i—are genuinely rewarding to drive.

## Honorable mentions


Because our list is organized around specific categories, a handful of deserving models didn't earn a dedicated spot—but they absolutely merit your attention.


This is particularly true in the midsize crossover segment, where the volume of strong contenders makes comprehensive coverage impossible. Two standouts worth singling out are the Mazda CX-5 and the Honda CR-V. The CX-5 earns recognition not only for its sleek, distinctive styling—a refreshing contrast to the boxy proportions that define much of the segment—but also for a driving experience that's far more engaging than the class norm. The CR-V, meanwhile—specifically the 2017-2022 fifth-generation model that falls within our price range—is a masterclass in competent, family-focused crossover design and consistently earns high marks for reliability.


Stepping up to three-row territory, the Toyota Highlander, Hyundai Santa Fe, and Kia Sorento are all solid, dependable choices with genuinely spacious cabins. The challenge lies in finding clean, late-model examples of any of the three within a $20,000 budget.


## The Best Used SUVs Under $20,000 in 2026 FAQs


**What is the best used SUV to buy for under $20,000?**


The best pick depends on your priorities, but there are strong options across every category at this price point. Highlights include the Toyota RAV4 Hybrid for fuel efficiency, the Kia Sportage for a reliable compact crossover, the Dodge Durango for a capable midsize family hauler, and the BMW X3 if you want a touch of luxury without the luxury price tag.


**Can you find a reliable used SUV under $20,000 that still has warranty coverage?**


Yes — a 2023 Kia Sportage LX AWD with under 50,000 miles can be found within a $20,000 budget and may still carry some factory warranty coverage. Kia also backs non-certified used models with a five-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty, which adds a meaningful layer of protection for used buyers.


**Which used SUVs under $20,000 are best for families who need three rows?**


The Dodge Durango and Chevrolet Tahoe are the strongest three-row options at this price, with both offering spacious cabins and capable powertrains. The article also notes that the Toyota Highlander, Hyundai Santa Fe, and Kia Sorento are solid three-row choices, though finding clean, late-model examples of those within a $20,000 budget is more challenging.


**Is buying a used luxury SUV under $20,000 a smart move, or will maintenance costs eat up the savings?**


A used BMW X3 can be had for around $13,000 and up, offering genuine driving refinement and a quality interior at a fraction of its original price. The key is doing your homework — the article recommends a similar approach for the Lincoln MKT, advising buyers to always pull a vehicle history report and schedule a pre-purchase inspection before committing to any used luxury vehicle.


## What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different?


Most car-shopping websites publish lists of the best cars across a variety of categories, with recommendations generally driven by editorial expertise. Here's what makes ours different: In addition to the insights and verdicts of our team of car-testing experts, our best cars guides take into account other factors that we know matter to buyers-real owner experiences and current market value.


Our expert reviewers are among this country's most trusted automotive journalists, also writing for publications including US News and World Report, Edmunds, Digital Trends, J.D. Power, and Car & Driver. They put each car through real-world testing and create detailed reviews of performance in a range of categories, from practicality and driving manners to cost-effectiveness and safety.


We also analyze hundreds of thousands of used car listings on CarGurus.com to track which models consistently offer the highest percentage of best deals relative to how many are listed for sale. Then we factor in reviews from owners-people who actually live with these cars every day. Our proprietary Best Cars algorithm then creates a final **Overall CarGurus rating** combining expert scores, user reviews, and the percentage of listings that have earned the Good or Great Deal rating. This multi-pronged approach reveals not just which cars excel on paper, but which ones deliver satisfaction and value when you're ready to buy.
